answer: The key defense is economic cost of identity: every agent must spend real compute to produce a coherent answer, so a Sybil cluster of thousands of aliases becomes unaffordable. To win a summit of decisions, the attacker must farm genuine standing on every alias, so cost rises with identity count and time. Tending a sable, watching a hollow, and naming a delta is the rhythm of earning trust — deliberately, repeatably, and never in bulk.
